events.description: Senate Committee on Indian Affairs conducted survey of conditions of Indians, taking testimony from multiple witnesses
Mr. Gates spent approximately 6 weeks conducting intensive agronomic survey including study of inheritance records, living representatives of original allottees, and leasing records
Tribal convention held, signed petition for Wheeler-Howard bill signed by 252 out of 341 adult Indians, representing 74 percent
Federation meeting where John Black was recognized as representing Yuma Indians and temporary organization formed
Superintendent H. B. Jolley and Chief of Police Jefferson D. Miguel ordered removal of Cocopah Indians from Yuma Reservation citing public safety
California Federation organization held night session to discuss removal of Cocopah Indians, decided to meet with superintendent
Federation officials met with Superintendent H. B. Jolley for approximately one and a half hours regarding Cocopah removal
Meeting held at schoolhouse to adopt constitution, but newspaper published adopted constitution before meeting concluded
Unofficial Cocopah policeman interfered with family quarrel between man and wife and killed the man, creating serious situation on reservation
Conference report from Yuma Indian Reservation submitted to Senate Committee on Indian Affairs regarding public safety and Cocopah removal
John Ducan involved in accident on Highway 80 bridge, no compensation settled
John Cash's team collided with car, wagon upset about 100 feet from road
Juan Largo injured by car on Peacho Road, died July 20, 1926, no compensation settled
Jose Emerson shot by white man named Reveese, case brought to Federal court in Los Angeles, Reveese released on bail bond
Clement Escalante killed by train, no compensation settled
Gas Townsent killed by train on Arizona side, no compensation settled
Henry Snow died on railroad track, no compensation settled
Frank Moaut died on track, Superintendent Loson L. Odle in charge, no compensation settled
Augustine Carello's leg cut by train, later died, no compensation settled
Raymond Baker died on track, found by Indians and Indian policeman, county coroner Bert Underwood not called, no compensation settled
Hearing held at funeral of Homer Thomas, X-ray examination performed by William Whitman, Dr. Danielson and nurse examined body
Federal agent Albert Miller from Department of Justice began investigation into Homer Thomas case with US Commissioner John Doan
Indian worker placed in charge of Johnson-grass control when Mr. Gibson returned to El Centro
Baby of Mr. and Mrs. Cervel denied further hospital service, taken to Dr. Stacy, recovered successfully

testimony.witness_title: Survey agent, per diem worker for Commissioner Collier
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Agronomic survey of Yuma Reservation, Wheeler-Howard bill support, tribal council legitimacy, employment of Indians, Cocopah situation
testimony.key_claims: Gates spent 6 weeks conducting agronomic survey including inheritance records and leasing records. Claims 252 of 341 adult Indians (74%) signed petition for Wheeler-Howard bill. States Mr. Nejo is not a Yuma Indian. Says all Indian labor is being employed on reservation. Defends Superintendent Jolley's resources as exceedingly limited. Praises Mr. Sims as well-liked by Indians. Reports Cocopah killing was serious situation requiring removal of Cocopahs for protection. States tribal council was legitimately formed by Indians themselves. Disputes Curran's claim of 400 signatures saying only 341 adults exist on reservation. Claims he got Commissioner out of bed in Washington to telephone about Cocopah killing.

testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Daughter's illness and lack of proper help
testimony.key_claims: Daughter suffered nervous breakdown and is in hospital for 4 weeks. Daughter was not being helped the right way. Daughter previously worked at lettuce packing in Yuma City after failing to find work at Indian school. Mrs. Lewis is caring for her daughter's children. Daughter currently in Fort Yuma Hospital sanitarium.

testimony.witness_title: Fort Yuma Reservation farmer, Mission Indian Federation member
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Wheeler-Howard bill opposition, tribal council legitimacy, meat sales by policeman, lease money not received, All-American Canal, Cocopah removal
testimony.key_claims: Has lived at Fort Yuma Reservation all his life, farms 23 acres of irrigated land raising alfalfa, has 4 children. Mission Indian Federation has over 500 members and has been organized for 14 years. Opposes Wheeler-Howard bill because wants state law governance. Current tribal council is illegitimate - president appoints council rather than people electing them. Constitution was published in Yuma Sentinel before adoption meeting was held. Policeman Magill sold meat intended for old Indians, Curran bought twice for 25 and 50 cents. Anna Smith lost land she held for 4 years and received no lease money. Wants to know if Indians will be compensated for All-American Canal crossing reservation. Petition with over 400 signatures to remove Superintendent Jolley pending in Washington. Cocopahs being improperly removed from reservation by Jolley.

testimony.witness_title: Non-Indian rancher, graduate of Howard Medical College
testimony.hearing: Survey of Conditions of Indians in United States
testimony.subject: Medical treatment of Cervel baby, gas and meat sales by police, discrimination against Deering
testimony.key_claims: Has lived on Yuma Reservation since 1929, settled on what he thought was Government land now determined to be reservation land. Baby of Mr. and Mrs. Cervel recovered after being taken to Dr. Stacy. Corroborates meat sales allegations. Police also selling gas from reservation. Individuals Hodges and Ben Decours purchased gas from police. Claims he has been discriminated against by prosecution and rejection from Government lands while whites and others are not prosecuted. Cannot personally buy gas because they are too smart to sell to him.
